chunks: Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah al-Barqi narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father Muhammad ibn Khalid, who linked it up through a chain of narrators to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him):

He said: The kings of the whole earth were four: two believers and two disbelievers. As for the two believers, they were Solomon son of David (peace be upon them both) and Dhul-Qarnayn. And the two disbelievers were Nimrod and Bakht al-Nasr. And the name of Dhul-Qarnayn was Abdullah ibn Dahhak ibn Ma'd.
ai.seo_question: Who are the four kings of the earth mentioned in Shia tradition, and which two were believers?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq categorizes these four archetypal rulers to illustrate the spectrum of faith and power, placing Solomon and Dhul-Qarnayn as models of righteous sovereignty and Nimrod and Nebuchadnezzar as exemplars of tyranny. This classification underscores the Shia scholarly view that political authority is validated by its alignment with divine truth, a theme deeply rooted in the Quranic narratives of these figures. The identification of Dhul-Qarnayn as Abdullah ibn Dahhak provides specific historical grounding often cited in exegetical traditions.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 4-130 Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Abdullah ibn Ahmad ibn Aba Abdullah al-Barqy narrated that his father quoted Ahmad ibn Aba Abdullah, on the authority of his father Muhammad ibn Khalid who linked it up through a chain of narrators to Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB), “

There were four kings on the Earth: two of the believers and two of the atheists. The two of the believers were Solomon - the son of David (MGB) and Zul-Qarnayn. The name of Zul-Qarnayn was Abdullah ibn Zahhak ibn Ma’d. The two atheists were Nimrood and Bakht ul-Nasr.”
